column2: The new drill is a hard one: pikes and halberds in close order, handgunners firing by ranks, a charge of horse to test the line. You ride the front yourself to show the men how it is done. A horse shies, a pike swings wide, and the next thing you know you are on your back in the mud with the surgeon kneeling over you.
The wound will heal. The drill goes on.
I will carry this mark for the rest of my days.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

A word from the drill yard: I was hurt while putting the men through a new formation. It is a clean wound and the surgeon says I will mend. The drill goes on without me until I can sit a horse again.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

My liege,

A word from the drill yard: I was hurt while putting the men through a new formation, and the surgeon could not save all of me. I am still your marshal and I will still serve, though I will never again lead a charge the way I did.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Such is the price of a strong army.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] keeps the finest soldiers in the province, and everyone knows why. [From.GetSheHeCap] has drill books of [From.GetHerHis] own, copied from veterans of a dozen campaigns: how to hold a square against cavalry, how to march a column through a forest without losing half of it. If [From.GetSheHe] could be talked into sharing them...
The lord will be asked to share the drill books.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], marshal of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has called on you with wine and compliments. What [From.GetSheHe] really wants are your drill books, which have cost you years of campaigning to put together.
Take them, and use them well.
Some secrets stay in the family.
The marshal will learn the lord's secrets.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent over [From.GetHerHis] drill books, bound in old leather and full of notes in the margins. Half of it you knew already. The other half will change the way the army fights.
My liege must hear of this generosity.
Your liege will gain the secrets.

My liege,

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has shared [FromFrom.GetHerHis] drill books with me, and I have already begun teaching their lessons to the men. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] deserves your thanks.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

The drills of the past months have paid off. Word has spread that the liege's marshal feeds the men well and pays on time, and fresh levies keep turning up at the muster: farmers' sons, discharged mercenaries and a few men nobody asks too many questions about.
The province will refill its levies faster.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] reports that the drill has drawn fresh men to the muster in [From.Location.GetName]. The levies there will be quick to fill again.

You have come to drill the levies of [From.Location.GetName], but one of the lords there keeps finding reasons why [From.GetHerHis] men cannot come: the harvest, a fever, a broken bridge. Nobody believes a word of it. [From.GetSheHeCap] simply does not want [From.GetHerHis] men learning to march to the liege's drum.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] writes, in the name of your liege, that your levies are to report for drill without further delay. The tone is not friendly.
My men stay on my land.
The marshal will write to the liege.

My liege,

[From.GetTitledFirstName] refuses to send [From.GetHerHis] levies to the drill. I have done what I can, but [From.GetSheHe] answers my letters with excuses and insults. The men of [FromFrom.Location.GetName] will be slow to answer your call to arms until this is settled.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

Word went round the longhouses that the liege wants fighting men, and they came: young warriors who have never taken a head, old ones who have run out of plunder, outlaws who want their names back. They are eager, they are hungry and they are already asking where the raiding is.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has brought a war band to your hall, raised from every corner of the land. They will follow you wherever there is loot, but they will not sit idle for long.
Then let us find them something to burn.

The raiders [From.GetTitledFirstName] raised for you have sat by your fires for months, eating your food and waiting for the raid you promised. Now they have had enough. Before they go home they want what they are owed, and they make it clear that they will take it one way or another.
Pay them and be rid of them.

Harvest was good in [Root.Location.GetName], and you made sure the liege's share was counted twice and collected once, with a little extra for the roads, the bridges and the walls that nobody will ever see built. The peasants grumbled, but they paid. A heavy chest is ready to go home.
Your liege will receive the tithe.
A chest arrives from [From.GetTitledFirstName], sealed with your steward's mark: a tithe from [From.Location.GetName], squeezed out of the peasants with the usual care.

The tax rolls have been read out in the square once too often. This time the crowd does not scatter. Someone throws a stone, someone else a pitchfork, and the whole village surges towards you, shouting that they will hang the steward from the church bell.
You make it to your horse with the mob at your heels and do not stop until you see the walls of the castle. Your dignity is somewhere back in the mud, along with your hat.
The mob catches up with you at the edge of the village. By the time the guards beat them back you have been dragged through the mud and given a beating you will feel for months.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] was attacked by peasants while collecting taxes in [From.Location.GetName], and badly hurt.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] was dragged off [From.GetHerHis] horse by peasants while collecting taxes in [From.Location.GetName], and beaten to death in the street.

You have squeezed [Root.Location.GetName] hard this year, and it shows. Granaries stand empty, the taverns are full of angry talk, and the bailiffs say men are meeting in the woods at night. The liege's taxes will be paid, but not gladly.

Word comes from [From.Location.GetName]: [From.GetTitledFirstName], the steward of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has taxed the province so hard that the peasants are close to rising. Your own lands there may not stay quiet.

My liege,

The people of [From.Location.GetName] are close to revolt over the taxes. The money is coming in, but the lords of the province blame you for it, and so do the peasants.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
They will pay all the same.

Among the masons on the walls of [Root.Location.GetName] you have found a true master: a grey old builder who learned his trade on the walls of a great city and can tell a bad stone just by tapping it. With him at your side, every work you oversee will go faster.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

I have taken a master builder into service. The works in [From.Location.GetName] are already going faster, and the people are glad of the work.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

Something is wrong with the works in [Root.Location.GetName]. Scaffolding collapses overnight, mortar will not set, and carts of good stone go missing on the road. The masons whisper that one of the local lords does not want the liege building here.
The lord will decide what to do.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], the steward of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], is building in [From.Location.GetName], right under your nose. If the work goes well, your liege will be stronger here, and you will be weaker. A few bribed masons could change that.
Pay the masons to botch it.
A whole section of the new wall has come down in the night, and half the masons have run off with their wages. Someone paid for this.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

The works in [From.Location.GetName] have been sabotaged. It will take a year to make good what was lost.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

Your agents have followed the money behind the sabotage in [FromFrom.Location.GetName]. The bribed masons all drink in the same tavern, and the man who paid them wears the colours of [From.GetTitledFirstName].
Your liege will learn who it was.

My liege,

The sabotage of your works was paid for by [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]. I have the masons' confessions if you need them.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
The people of [Root.Location.GetName] have given up the old ways. They speak our tongue, keep our feasts and send their sons to our wars. The land is ours now, and not only on the map.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] reports that the people of [From.Location.GetName] have taken up our ways.
Not everyone in [Root.Location.GetName] wants to be settled. A band of locals ambushes you on the road, and you get away with a blade in your side.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] was ambushed and wounded by locals while settling [From.Location.GetName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] has not given up.

You have spent months telling the deeds of [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] in every hall and camp of the land, and the tales have spread. Now young warriors come every day, wanting to fight for a lord whose name is in the songs.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] arrives at the head of a crowd of warriors, all of them drawn by tales of your deeds. They want to fight for you, and they want to do it soon.
The warriors drawn by your fame have waited a year for a war that never came. One by one they have packed up and gone home, telling everyone they meet that your legend is all talk.

[event_target:tribute_giver.GetTitledFirstName] keeps a rich camp in [Root.Location.GetName], and [event_target:tribute_giver.GetSheHe] could easily spare more for [event_target:tribute_asker.GetTitledFirstName]. Of course, [event_target:tribute_giver.GetSheHe] may not see it that way.
The lord will be asked for a year's income.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], steward of [event_target:tribute_asker.GetTitledFirstName], has come to your camp. [From.GetSheHeCap] wants a year's income on top of what you already pay, and makes it clear that this is not a request.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has paid the extra tribute, with very bad grace.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] has squeezed a year's income out of [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName].
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has refused to pay any more tribute and had you thrown out of the camp.
The liege will hear of this.
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has refused your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s demand for extra tribute.

A long evening of good wine, old stories and well-placed compliments. By the end of it, one of the lords of [Root.Location.GetName] is laughing at all your jokes and saying that [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] must be a fine ruler to keep such a charming chancellor.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], chancellor of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has spent the evening at your table. You cannot remember when you last enjoyed a guest so much, and you find yourself thinking more kindly of [From.GetHerHis] master.

My liege,

[From.GetTitledFirstName] now thinks very well of you. It cost me only a cask of good wine and a long evening of listening to [From.GetHerHis] stories.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
It was meant to be a friendly visit. Somewhere between the second cup and the third, you made a joke about the lord's mother, and the room went quiet. You left before the soup was served.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], the chancellor of a foreign lord, sat at your table and insulted your family to your face. You will not forget the master who sent such an envoy.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], the chancellor of your own liege, sat at your table and insulted your family to your face. If this is what the liege thinks of you, you will remember it.

My liege,

I regret to tell you that my visit to [From.GetTitledFirstName] went badly. Words were said that should not have been said, and [From.GetSheHe] now blames you for them.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

The archives of [Root.Location.GetName] are full of old deeds and grants, and nobody has read most of them in a hundred years. With a sharp knife, a steady hand and the right ink, you can make one of them say that the land belongs to [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName].

A friend at the court of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] has sent word: [From.GetHerHis] chancellor, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has "discovered" an old deed giving [From.Liege.GetHerHim] a claim on [target_title.GetName]. The ink is barely dry.

My liege,

I have found an old deed proving your right to the county of [target_title.GetName], held by [From.GetTitledFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] already knows of it and will not be happy. Pressing the claim will cost gold for the lawyers and some of your good name.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

My liege,

I have found an old deed proving your right to the duchy of [target_title.GetName], held by [From.GetTitledFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] already knows of it and is furious. Pressing a claim this large will cost a great deal of gold and a good part of your good name.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

My liege,

You want a crown, and I have found one for you: an old deed proving your right to the kingdom of [target_title.GetName], held by [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Pressing it will cost a fortune and much of your good name, but a crown is a crown.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
Let it go. This is beneath me.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has pressed the forged claim on [target_title.GetName]. Everybody knows the deed is false, and [From.GetSheHe] does not care.
You have been careless. A clerk you paid to look the other way has talked, and now the lord of [Root.Location.GetName] knows exactly what you have been doing in the archives.
The lord will decide what to do with you.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], the chancellor of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has been forging deeds in your archives to steal your land. You have the clerk's confession. Now what?
Send [From.GetHerHim] some gold to forget about it.
The chancellor will be offered a bribe.
You wake in the dark to a hand over your mouth. There are three of them, and they do not say a word.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] was found dead in [From.GetHerHis] bed this morning. Nobody saw anything.
The assassins you hired were caught on the stairs and fled. [From.GetTitledFirstName] is alive, and now very much on guard.
A purse arrives with a short note from [From.GetTitledFirstName]: "For your trouble. Perhaps your work in my archives is finished?"
Take the gold and stop for a while.
The lord will know you took it.
The lord will get the gold back.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has taken your gold. The forgeries will stop, at least for a while.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent your purse back unopened.

Your chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been murdered in [From.GetHerHis] bed. Nobody saw the killers, but [From.GetSheHe] had been working in [From.Location.GetName], and someone there clearly wanted [From.GetHerHim] gone.
One of the lords of [Root.Location.GetName] is proud, touchy and convinced that his liege does not value him. With a word here and a rumour there, you can make sure he never forgives his master.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], chancellor of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has told you things about your liege that you can never unhear: slights, insults, plans to give your lands to others. It all makes sense now.
The lord's liege will hear of it.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has turned cold and sullen towards you, and tells anyone who will listen that you have wronged [From.GetHerHim]. Someone has been poisoning [From.GetHerHis] mind.

My liege,

[From.GetTitledFirstName] now hates [From.GetHerHis] own liege. A few words in the right ear were enough.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
You were careless. One of the lords of [Root.Location.GetName] has found out what you have been whispering to [From.GetHerHis] neighbours.
The lord will deal with you.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], chancellor of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has been caught spreading lies to set the lords of [From.Location.GetName] against their liege.
You have been seized and thrown into a dungeon for your schemes. The cell is cold and the guards laugh at you.
Your chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been caught sowing dissent abroad and thrown into a dungeon. Everyone is talking about it.

My liege,

I have caught [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName], the chancellor of [FromFrom.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], trying to turn your lords against you, and thrown [FromFrom.GetHerHim] in my dungeon.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

My liege,

I have caught [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName], the chancellor of [FromFrom.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], trying to turn your lords against you.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has written to complain that your chancellor has been spreading lies among [From.GetHerHis] neighbours.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has learned that your chancellor tried to turn [From.GetHerHis] lords against [From.GetHerHim], and has written you a very angry letter.
You have sat by the fires of the clan of [Root.Location.Owner.GetTitledFirstName] for weeks, sharing their kumis and telling stories of the khan's generosity. They are starting to listen.
Your chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] has spent weeks among the clan of [target_chief.GetTitledFirstName], and they now speak well of your clan.

For years you have preached in the squares of [Root.Location.GetName], burned the idols of the old shrines and sat at the bedsides of the dying. Today the last of the old priests came to you, knelt, and asked to be received into the true faith. The province is [Root.Religion.GetName] at last.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

[From.Location.GetName] has turned to the true faith. The old shrines are cold, and our temples are full.

Your servant in faith,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Word comes that [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s Lord Spiritual has brought a province of your realm to the true faith.
[Root.Location.GetName] has many souls who still cling to false gods. One of them has come to you with doubts, and over many long talks you have answered every one.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has shown you the error of your old beliefs. You cannot go back to them now.

My liege,

I have brought [From.GetTitledFirstName] to the true faith.

Your servant in faith,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been converted by a foreign Lord Spiritual and now follows the [From.Religion.GetName] faith.
The unbelievers of [Root.Location.GetName] have had enough of your sermons and your burnings. A mob with clubs and torches is coming up the road to your chapel.
You escape through the back of the chapel with the mob at your heels. The chapel burns behind you.
The mob catches you on the steps of the chapel. By the time the guards come you are lying in your own blood.
Your liege will hear of it.
Your Lord Spiritual [From.GetTitledFirstName] was attacked by unbelievers in [From.Location.GetName] and badly hurt. That a priest of yours can be beaten in your own lands makes you look weak.
Your Lord Spiritual [From.GetTitledFirstName] was killed by a mob of unbelievers in [From.Location.GetName]. [From.GetHerHis] chapel was burned with [From.GetHerHim].
[suspected_heretic.GetTitledFirstName] skips the holy days, mocks the priests at table and was seen reading forbidden books. Nobody else seems to care, but you know heresy when you see it.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has denounced you as a heretic from the pulpit! A few late prayers and a joke at dinner, and now the whole realm is whispering about you.
Your Lord Spiritual has accused [From.GetTitledFirstName] of heresy, and [From.GetSheHe] begs you to clear [From.GetHerHis] name. You must choose whom to believe.
Your Lord Spiritual will be overruled.
The lord will be branded a heretic.
Your Lord Spiritual will be upheld.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has cleared you of heresy. Your name is clean again.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has refused to believe your accusation and told you to mind your own sermons.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has branded you a heretic. People cross the street to avoid you now, and the priests will not give you their blessing.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has upheld your accusation. The heretic has been branded for all to see.
Your inquisition has stirred up [Root.Location.GetName]. The unbelievers hide their priests, bar their doors when you pass and spit on your servants. Something is going to break.
Word comes from [From.Location.GetName]: the inquisition of [From.GetTitledFirstName] has the province close to religious riots. Your lands there may not stay quiet.

My liege,

The unbelievers of [From.Location.GetName] are close to rising against the faith. The lords of the province blame you for my work.

Your servant in faith,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
The fanatics who held [Root.Location.GetName] have been broken. Their preachers are in chains or hanging from the town gate, and their followers have gone back to their fields.

My liege,

The fanatics of [From.Location.GetName] are no more. Order and the true faith have been restored.

Your servant in faith,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
You have spent many evenings with one of the priest-lords of [Root.Location.GetName], talking theology over good wine. He has come to see the liege as a true friend of the faith.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been a fine companion these past weeks: learned, devout and full of praise for [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]. Perhaps you have misjudged the liege.

My liege,

[From.GetTitledFirstName] now thinks well of you.

Your servant in faith,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
The head of the faith is far away, and his envoys take more than they give. One of the priest-lords of [Root.Location.GetName] has started to see that you are right.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has told you things about the head of the faith that you did not want to hear: the bribes, the luxury, the favours sold for gold. You will never look at [From.Religion.GetName] the same way again.

My liege,

[From.GetTitledFirstName] no longer trusts the head of the faith. [From.GetSheHeCap] will look to you before [From.GetSheHe] looks to them.

Your servant in faith,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
A wandering scholar has come to you, full of new ideas about canals, mills and medicine. He has read the old books of half the Old World and wants a patron. He does not come cheap.

My liege,

I am sending you a scholar of rare learning. He asks for a generous purse, but what he knows could change the realm.

Your servant in faith,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

Your studies have taken you deep into the old texts, and the more you read, the less you believe what the temple teaches. The commentaries contradict each other, the old prophets say things the temple never mentions, and the truth, you are sure now, is something else.
Your Lord Spiritual [From.GetTitledFirstName] has fallen into heresy. [From.GetSheHeCap] has not hidden it, and soon the whole realm will know.
[From.GetSheHeCap] is right. I will follow openly.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has secretly come round to your beliefs, but asks you to keep up the old faith in public, as [From.GetSheHe] does, until the time is right.
I will not hide the truth.
You have handed out bread and coin in the liege's name at every temple of [Root.Location.GetName]. The beggars bless [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], and so do the lords who saw it.
The court priest of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] has fed the poor of your lands for weeks. A liege so generous deserves your respect.
Thanks to the charity of your court priest [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName], [From.GetTitledFirstName] now thinks well of you.
Word spread that you would hand out bread at the temple of [Root.Location.GetName], and half the province came. When the bread ran out, the crowd surged forward.
You escaped over the temple wall with your robes torn and your turban gone. The whole city saw it.
The crowd knocked you down and walked over you. You will be a long time healing.
Your court priest [From.GetTitledFirstName] was trampled by the hungry crowd while handing out alms in [From.Location.GetName].
Your court priest [From.GetTitledFirstName] was trampled to death by the hungry crowd while handing out alms in [From.Location.GetName].
The purse for the poor is heavy this month, and nobody counts what goes out of it. Who would miss a few coins?
Give it to the poor, as is right.
Your court priest [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been dipping into the alms meant for the poor.
Take a share and say nothing.
At every temple of the realm the people pray for the health of [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]. You made sure of it.
Your court priest [From.GetTitledFirstName] has had the whole realm pray for you.
Your sermons have set the young warriors on fire. They come from every camp and village to fight for the gods and for [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName].
[From.GetTitledFirstName] brings a host of zealots to your hall, burning to fight for the faith.
The zealots who came to fight for the faith have waited a year for a holy war that never came. They have gone home, and they are saying the gods have left you.

A bribed servant, a letter lifted from a saddlebag, a few coins in the right taverns: it took weeks, but I have it now. [spy_plotter.GetTitledName] is plotting, and I know exactly what. I should be careful. A plotter who learns they have been found out is a dangerous thing.
Knowledge is a blade. Now to use it.

My steward came to me pale this morning: a servant has been selling my letters, and the buyer was [From.GetTitledName], spymaster to [From.Liege.GetTitledName]. The spymaster knows what I am planning. The spymaster is also only one person, and accidents happen in dark streets.
Lie low and hope it blows over.

The knife came out of the dark as I crossed the yard. I felt it scrape my ribs before I threw the man off and he fled over the wall. I know who sent him. [From.GetTitledName] wants me dead because of what I know.
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] learns of the plot and the attempt on your life.

My Liege,

I have found proof that [spy_plotter.GetTitledName] is plotting, and when [spy_plotter.GetSheHe] learned of it, assassins came for me in the night. I live, by luck and a quick hand. What should be done with the plotter?

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledName]
Drag the plot into the light!

A rider brought a letter from [From.GetTitledName] today. It said only that my plans are known to [From.GetHerHim], every one of them, and that [From.GetSheHe] will be watching me. The seal was broken when it reached me. I suspect half the court has read it.

I was asking the wrong questions in the wrong part of town, and someone noticed. Five men with cudgels and knives are waiting at the end of the alley, and two more behind me. [killer_target.GetTitledName] pays well, it seems.
I fled over rooftops and through a tannery, and lost them in the stink. My dignity stayed in the gutter, but I live.
I fought my way clear, but not before one of them opened my arm to the bone. A barber sewed it shut by candlelight. I should write to my liege.

My Liege,

I was set upon by hired thugs while about your business. I took a wound but will recover. Whoever paid them is afraid of what I might find.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledName]
My spymaster, [From.GetTitledName], was found in an alley with a dozen stab wounds. Whatever [From.GetSheHe] had learned died too.

I have it on good authority that [spy_faction_target.GetTitledName] has joined a faction against [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]. Better still, I know a few things about [spy_faction_target.GetTitledFirstName] that could make [spy_faction_target.GetHerHim] think again.

My Liege,

[spy_faction_target.GetTitledName] has joined a faction against you. I have looked into [spy_faction_target.GetHerHis] life and habits, and there are ways to make [spy_faction_target.GetHerHim] reconsider. Tell me how you wish to proceed.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledName]

A letter from [From.GetTitledName] arrived today. It lists, in a clerk's tidy hand, things about my private life I had thought no one knew. At the end it suggests I leave my faction, or the list will be read aloud at court.

A letter from [From.GetTitledName] arrived today. It lists, in a clerk's tidy hand, things about my private life I had thought no one knew. At the end it suggests I join [From.GetHerHis] faction, or the list will be read aloud at court.
Let them talk. I do not bend.
[From.GetTitledName] has written to me asking, quite courteously, that I leave my faction for the good of the realm.
[From.GetTitledName] has written to me asking, quite courteously, that I join [From.GetHerHis] faction.
[From.GetTitledName] has written to me setting out, clause by clause, the oaths I swore and the laws I am breaking by sitting in a faction against our liege.
[From.GetTitledName] has written to me setting out, clause by clause, the old rights and laws [From.GetHerHis] faction means to defend.

[From.GetTitledName] has written to me. The letter is polite. It also mentions my children by name, the road they take to the chapel, and how dangerous the roads are these days. I am to leave my faction.
